title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
code_note: Official system repository inspected; it distinguishes this reusable memory package from the separate paper-evaluation repository. Neither was executed.
learning_signal: New observations and language-model judgments of relationships among notes.
mechanism: Constructs structured notes, links related memories, and updates older contextual descriptions when new information arrives. The evolving note network changes retrieval context without modifying model weights.
evaluation: The primary abstract reports comparisons with memory baselines across six foundation models.
limitations: This review covers the abstract and official memory-system page. Interpretation: reorganizing a memory store is a form of adaptation, but it is not sufficient evidence of growing procedural skill or reliable long-term retention.

title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Executable task validity, solution correctness, and task learnability rewards.
mechanism: A single model proposes and solves code-based tasks, with a code executor validating problems and answers. Reinforcement learning updates both roles while the generated task buffer supplies a changing curriculum.
evaluation: Experiments compare coding and mathematics reasoning across base-model families and scales, with ablations of task types and proposer design.
limitations: Zero data refers to new task and answer supervision during this training stage; the system starts from pretrained models and uses an engineered executor and task format. Curator interpretation: bounded benchmark gains do not establish unlimited improvement.

title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Repeated generated-data training with old data retained rather than replaced.
mechanism: Compares replacement of earlier datasets with accumulation of original and synthetic data. It supplies a linear-model analysis and generative-model experiments showing that the data-retention policy changes collapse behavior.
evaluation: The study includes small transformer language models on TinyStories, molecular diffusion, image variational autoencoders, and controlled analytical models.
limitations: The bounded-error theorem is for its stated linear setting, and retaining growing datasets changes resource requirements. Curator interpretation: these results challenge universal collapse claims without certifying arbitrary self-training or agent-memory loops.

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Reflection on generated trajectories, execution outcomes, and useful or harmful context entries.
mechanism: Separates generation, reflection, and curation to build an evolving playbook. Small structured updates and deduplication preserve reusable strategies without repeatedly rewriting the entire context.
evaluation: Experiments cover AppWorld and financial-analysis tasks; offline adaptation and sequential predict-then-update evaluation are reported separately.
limitations: Adaptation depends on the reflector extracting useful lessons and can accumulate noise. Online test-stream learning is a different protocol from evaluating a frozen agent on independent tasks.

title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Benchmark feedback and an archive of previously generated agent designs.
mechanism: A meta-agent writes new agent programs, evaluates them, and uses the growing archive to propose further designs. Code represents the prompts, control flow, and other components being searched.
evaluation: Experiments cover coding, science, and math, with reported transfer of discovered designs across tasks and models.
limitations: The meta-agent search procedure is fixed; improving a task agent is distinct from improving the mechanism that invents agents. The reported transfer remains bounded by the evaluated domains and models.

title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Execution scores on a validation subset and stored search experience.
mechanism: Searches over code-represented workflows using a Monte Carlo tree-search variant. An LLM changes prompts and connections between operations, while the tree retains feedback from prior candidates.
evaluation: Six QA, coding, and math datasets are divided into development and test subsets; the paper also compares execution costs and transfer between executor models.
limitations: The study focuses on reasoning tasks with accessible evaluators and commonly used operators. Search costs and repeated validation exposure should be considered separately from the inference cost of the selected workflow.

title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents
code_note: Official repository linked from arXiv and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Task success and memory-quality rewards, with penalties for redundant storage, tool use, and context growth.
mechanism: Trains an agent to select long-term memory edits and short-term context operations as tools. Three progressive stages and step-wise GRPO assign delayed task rewards to earlier memory decisions; the resulting policy manages external memory during use.
evaluation: Evaluates Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-4B agents on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, PDDL, BabyAI, and HotpotQA, with memory-quality, efficiency, and ablation comparisons.
limitations: The memory-operation vocabulary is fixed. The authors distinguish controlled cross-domain transfer from persistent real-user or long-term dialogue deployments, which remain future evaluation settings.

title: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training
code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
learning_signal: Environment terminal rewards, tree-search alternatives, and actor-selected error locations.
mechanism: Uses Monte Carlo tree search to pair unsuccessful and successful paths. The current actor selects a revision point, and spliced correction trajectories support iterative supervised training of an error-recovery policy.
evaluation: The authors test three training iterations on WebShop, ScienceWorld, and TextCraft, comparing task reward, recovery from truncated failures, and action-loop behavior.
limitations: Training also uses ShareGPT data and manually written revision connectors. The evaluated setup uses a specific backbone and reward-bearing environments; learning to revise a trajectory is distinct from modifying the learning algorithm.

title: Agent Workflow Memory
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Annotated offline trajectories or model-judged successful online task trajectories.
mechanism: Abstracts reusable subroutines from action trajectories and adds them to the agent context as workflow memory. It supports an offline store built from training examples and an online store updated after completed tasks.
evaluation: The authors evaluate Mind2Web and WebArena, including cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain splits and workflow-representation ablations.
limitations: Online memory admission uses a learned success evaluator, so stored workflows can inherit its errors. Interpretation: sequential test-time learning should be compared under the same task order and feedback access.

title: Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Solver self-consistency, tool-use incentives, diversity penalties, and pseudo-label-based executor rewards.
mechanism: Co-trains a curriculum agent and a tool-using executor in alternating stages. The proposer targets uncertain, diverse tasks, while filtered generated tasks and a code interpreter support executor updates.
evaluation: The paper tests two Qwen base-model sizes on mathematics and general-reasoning suites, comparing tool-enabled baselines and other self-evolving methods.
limitations: No new human-annotated training tasks are required, but pretrained weights, reward design, and tool infrastructure remain inputs. Curator interpretation: majority-derived pseudo-labels need independent correctness checks, and peak training scores are not evidence of indefinite improvement.

title: AgentDevel: Reframing Self-Evolving LLM Agents as Release Engineering
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Implementation-blind trace critiques, executable diagnosis, and per-task regression/fix outcomes.
mechanism: Externalizes improvement into a release pipeline that constructs one candidate at a time. Promotion emphasizes which previously passing tasks fail and which failing tasks are repaired.
evaluation: The abstract reports execution-heavy benchmark experiments with fewer regressions and auditable version histories.
limitations: This is an external improvement pipeline rather than in-agent autonomous learning. The abstract review does not establish the benchmark composition, statistical uncertainty, or protection against every regression.

title: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Task scores and an in-context performance predictor used to screen candidates.
mechanism: Defines interchangeable planning, reasoning, tool-use, and memory modules, then searches by evolving and recombining them. A performance predictor reduces evaluations of unpromising designs.
evaluation: The authors compare generated agents on six benchmarks spanning web, embodied, tool-use, and game tasks.
limitations: Optimization operates within predefined module interfaces and an external search framework. Curator interpretation: gains under these tasks do not establish unrestricted architectural invention or continual learning after deployment.

title: AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?
code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
learning_signal: Execution outcomes and model-generated feedback; ground-truth test labels are withheld from adaptation.
mechanism: Evaluates retained agent state under isolated domain streams, sequential domain shifts, and interleaved tasks, comparing each evolving agent with a no-evolution baseline.
evaluation: Crosses five methods with three model backbones and six benchmarks; method benefits vary with the model and stream composition.
limitations: The paper limits model-strength conclusions to its framework and selected benchmarks. Streaming performance is not proof of indefinite retention or deployment reliability.

title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
code_note: Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.
learning_signal: Grades from evaluator-held-out task data under fixed per-task budgets, with separate public feedback for inner optimization.
mechanism: Searches research-agent harness rewrites, retaining the best incumbent for further edits. The editable agent controls search and context management; the outer selection rule remains fixed.
evaluation: Reports seven accepted rewrites in the main eight-day run, transfer to ALE-Bench, MLE-Bench, FML-Bench and WeatherBench 2, and a separate comparison using an evolved agent as the outer optimizer.
limitations: The outer-optimizer comparison is inconclusive with three seeds per arm. Noisy grades can accept false improvements. Harness gains do not establish accelerating self-improvement or independent reproduction.

title: Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Game outcomes and search-improved move selections from self-play.
mechanism: Trains a policy/value network on games generated by its own search, then uses the updated network to improve subsequent search and play. This is an early concrete example of a coupled data-generation and policy-improvement loop.
evaluation: The authors evaluate playing strength against earlier Go programs, including the previously published champion-defeating AlphaGo.
limitations: The environment supplies exact rules, legal moves, and a reliable win/loss signal. Curator interpretation: success in this closed game does not establish open-ended language-agent learning.

title: ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience
code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
learning_signal: Completed execution trajectories accepted by an environment verifier, with action-validity feedback.
mechanism: After one scored attempt per task, a frozen copy of the initial model reads accepted experience with hindsight. Its token distributions train persistent LoRA adapters for subsequent tasks; invalid-action turns are removed from the privileged teacher input.
evaluation: The authors report success, interaction cost, ablations, and held-out scene transfer on ALFWorld and WebShop with two model sizes, plus AppWorld experiments.
limitations: The method needs an available verifier and update compute. WebShop adaptation accepts scores of at least 0.9 although reported exact success requires 1.0; outcome acceptance does not identify causally useful actions or prove a shortest solution.

title: AutoSkill: Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning via Skill Self-Evolution
code_note: Official repository linked by the paper and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Dialogue histories, recurring user preferences, corrections, and model judgments about extraction and merging.
mechanism: Extracts explicit instruction skills from interactions, retrieves them for later requests, and merges related updates into versioned skill artifacts. A persistent skill bank changes while the underlying language model stays fixed.
evaluation: The inspected v2 reports SkillBank statistics from four language/model subsets of WildChat and qualitative examples of extracted and repeatedly revised skills.
limitations: Artifact counts and case studies demonstrate construction and maintenance, not a controlled estimate of improved downstream task success or long-term retention. This AutoSkill is distinct from MUSE-Autoskill and similarly named video-QA work.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Describes an evolution loop through inputs, agent systems, environments, and optimizers, then maps techniques and domain-specific applications onto those components.
evaluation: Reviews methods alongside evaluation, safety, and ethical considerations.
limitations: Review coverage and categories reflect the authors’ literature selection; the framework does not itself demonstrate lifelong capability growth.

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Human-authored principles guide AI critiques, revisions, and preference judgments.
mechanism: Uses self-critiques and revisions for supervised learning, then learns a preference model from AI comparisons and optimizes the assistant with reinforcement learning. The process automates parts of supervision while retaining an externally chosen constitution.
evaluation: The authors report human evaluations of helpfulness and harmlessness for trained assistants.
limitations: The constitution and training procedure are designed externally. Curator interpretation: this supports AI-assisted alignment training, not unsupervised value discovery or a guarantee that safety persists through later self-modification.

title: CREATOR: Tool Creation for Disentangling Abstract and Concrete Reasoning of Large Language Models
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Problem specifications and execution feedback for tool creation and revision.
mechanism: Decomposes problem solving into tool design, implementation, execution, and revision so an agent can create tools beyond a fixed API inventory. It also examines reuse of created tools for knowledge transfer.
evaluation: The authors evaluate MATH, TabMWP, and the introduced Creation Challenge dataset, with tool-use and reasoning baselines.
limitations: Much of the framework concerns solving and repairing an individual problem. Interpretation: tool-transfer experiments should be separated from claims of a continually improving cross-task agent.

title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Coding-benchmark outcomes and evaluation logs used to propose self-edits.
mechanism: A coding agent rewrites its own implementation, and an archive retains runnable variants as possible parents for later edits. This permits exploration beyond the latest or immediately best-performing agent.
evaluation: The paper evaluates SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot subsets, ablates self-improvement and archive exploration, and studies transfer across foundation models.
limitations: Foundation models, archive management, and parent selection remain fixed in the inspected study. Staged search and evaluation use benchmark subsets, so the reported curves should not be interpreted as a fully separate hidden-task deployment evaluation.

title: Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Proposer–solver feedback grounded in an external search environment.
mechanism: Co-evolves a proposer that generates diverse, challenging questions and a search-enabled solver. Hop-grouped policy optimization shares baselines among structurally similar questions to reduce training overhead.
evaluation: The authors compare the trained search agents with supervised alternatives on several question-answering benchmarks.
limitations: Without training data means without human-annotated task data, not without external information: the search engine supplies a knowledge environment. This abstract-level review does not independently test search freshness, citation fidelity, or long-term robustness.

title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: A developer-specified metric and examples used to bootstrap demonstrations.
mechanism: Represents language-model pipelines as declarative modules and compiles demonstrations for their component prompts. The reusable artifact is an optimized pipeline configuration.
evaluation: The paper studies math reasoning and retrieval-based question-answering pipelines, comparing compiled programs with hand-written prompts and demonstrations.
limitations: Compilation is externally configured optimization; the paper does not establish an agent that autonomously maintains learning after deployment. The proceedings landing page uses a title variant ending in State-of-the-Art Pipelines.

title: Building Self-Evolving Agents via Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning: A Framework and Benchmark
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Benchmark task success, long-term retention through environmental tools, and proactive initiative metrics.
mechanism: Defines experience-driven lifelong learning around exploration, memory, skill abstraction, and internalization, and introduces StuLife as a stateful simulated student-life environment. Its framework is a research agenda and evaluation setting rather than a single demonstrated learning algorithm.
evaluation: The inspected preprint v6 resets agent context between tasks; retained information must be explicitly stored and retrieved through environmental tools such as calendars and drafts. The later published abstract additionally describes context-engineering comparisons, whose full protocol was not reviewed here.
limitations: The selected full-text review concerns the preprint v6 baseline in a designed simulation, not a trained lifelong learner’s learning curve. The renamed Findings of EMNLP 2026 version has verified publication metadata; its full experimental revision was not inspected.

title: EvoAgentX: An Automated Framework for Evolving Agentic Workflows
code_note: Official repository inspected; the original URL redirects to ANative-Lab/EvoAgentX. No code was installed or executed.
learning_signal: Task evaluations used by integrated prompt and workflow optimizers.
mechanism: Integrates workflow generation and execution with optimization methods including TextGrad, AFlow, and MIPRO. The framework supports changes to prompts, tool configurations, and workflow topology.
evaluation: The authors evaluate QA, coding, and math workflows on HotpotQA, MBPP, and MATH, with additional GAIA tasks.
limitations: Integration of optimizers is distinct from demonstrating a new self-improvement mechanism. Curator interpretation: benchmark gains under configured optimization do not establish continual autonomous adaptation in deployment.

title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Local workload feedback and evidence-guided validation of combined program changes.
mechanism: Different clients evolve copies of a shared harness on local tasks. A server combines compatible program adaptations and redistributes the result so later evolution can reuse discoveries from other clients.
evaluation: The revised abstract reports five experimental settings and ablations separating adaptation composition from selecting a single specialist.
limitations: The theoretical results are conditional on assumptions about retaining and composing improvements. Curator interpretation: sharing code adaptations without raw workloads does not by itself establish a formal privacy guarantee.

title: EvoX: Meta-Evolution for Automated Discovery
code_note: Official SkyDiscover repository linked by the paper and inspected; it also contains other algorithms. Not executed.
learning_signal: Task-evaluator scores, execution artifacts, and changes in population performance over search windows.
mechanism: Co-evolves candidate programs and the search strategy that selects parents, variation operators, and examples. Stagnation triggers strategy revisions informed by earlier strategies and current population state.
evaluation: Evaluates 196 mathematical, systems, and algorithmic optimization tasks, with three runs and generally 100 iterations for open-framework comparisons.
limitations: Search adapts within each optimization problem; cross-task lifelong retention is not established. AlphaEvolve comparisons use published scores with an undisclosed iteration budget. Evaluators and outer monitoring rules remain supplied.

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Task outcomes and model-generated comparisons of successful and unsuccessful trajectories.
mechanism: Collects training-task trajectories, contrasts successes and failures to extract reusable textual insights, and retrieves relevant experiences for new tasks. Learning changes the external experience and insight stores without updating the base model.
evaluation: The paper evaluates HotpotQA, ALFWorld, and WebShop, examines insight and retrieval ablations, and studies transfer from question answering to fact verification.
limitations: The investigated environments have textual observations and are deterministic. The authors note that larger lifelong insight stores would need additional retrieval beyond fitting all insights into context.

title: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Intervenes on raw and condensed experience to test whether an agent’s decisions causally depend on the experience it receives.
evaluation: Across several frameworks, backbones, and environments, the authors find that condensed experience can be ignored or misinterpreted even when raw experience influences behavior.
limitations: The interventions support conclusions within the tested systems. High end-task scores alone do not reveal whether the intended learning pathway caused a gain.

title: FlexA-Mem: Budget-Adaptive Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: New history records and current queries; rendering follows a fixed rule.
mechanism: Keeps an immutable history store and constructs a query-specific context from a timeline plus retrieved detail under a fixed token budget. Its fixed rendering rules provide a useful baseline for learned memory systems.
evaluation: The abstract reports AppWorld task-completion experiments and LongMemEval and LoCoMo QA, including an unused-task evaluation with predictions fixed beforehand.
limitations: The method adapts the presented context rather than learning its own update policy. It is included as an adjacent comparison for separating memory access gains from agent self-learning.

title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
code_note: Author-linked public repository page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Collaborative interaction traces and environment feedback, including task success or failure.
mechanism: Organizes multi-agent experience into linked interaction, query, and insight graphs. Bidirectional traversal retrieves abstract guidance and condensed role-specific histories; completed episodes update the hierarchy for later queries.
evaluation: Reports five benchmarks spanning embodied action, knowledge QA, and games, using three language-model backbones and three multi-agent frameworks, alongside cost and component analyses.
limitations: This changes the memory supplied to existing teams; it does not establish autonomous redesign of their coordination or models. The authors leave broader domain validation, including medical QA, for future work.

title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks
code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
learning_signal: Training tasks with controlled supervision; held-out rules are recombinations of training evidence.
mechanism: Distributes hidden business rules across training tasks and recombines them in held-out tasks, using an automated pipeline to construct environments and deterministic graders.
evaluation: Compares agent/model combinations and supervision types on generated enterprise workflow tasks and analyzes rule transfer.
limitations: Construction calibrates task groups partly for an expected improvement range, which can favor detectable learning gains. These are generated business scenarios, not a live enterprise deployment study.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
code_note: Official repository inspected; not executed. The ACM record was inaccessible during this review, so the catalog status conservatively describes the inspected preprint.
learning_signal: Observed simulated events and model-generated reflections.
mechanism: Stores experiences, synthesizes higher-level reflections, and retrieves relevant memories to plan behavior in a simulated town. The accumulated state shapes subsequent actions and social interactions.
evaluation: The authors assess behavioral believability and emergent coordination in a sandbox populated by simulated agents, including architecture ablations.
limitations: Believability is a different outcome from task competence or factual correctness. This is an adjacent foundation for persistent reflective memory, not a demonstration of open-ended capability improvement.

title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Execution trajectories, textual critiques, and candidate validation scores.
mechanism: Reflects on traces to propose prompt edits and selects complementary candidates using a Pareto-based population. The learned instructions alter a compound system while keeping its model weights fixed.
evaluation: The final proceedings abstract reports comparisons with GRPO and MIPROv2 across six tasks, plus inference-time code optimization.
limitations: The headline comparison concerns the reported models, tasks, and budgets; it is not a general ranking of prompt optimization and reinforcement learning. Curator interpretation: total evaluation and reflector costs matter alongside rollout counts.

title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: High-level objectives and task-performance feedback.
mechanism: Lets an LLM-based agent inspect and revise its own logic through a self-referential learning framework. The editable artifact is the agent program rather than the underlying language-model weights.
evaluation: The paper reports experiments in mathematical reasoning and agent tasks, with performance, efficiency, and generalization comparisons.
limitations: Empirical task gains are not formal proofs that a modification is beneficial. The ACL proceedings title uses Recursively Self-Improvement; it is the same research lineage as the linked arXiv record.

title: Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Shared experience across a group of agent variants and coding-task evaluations.
mechanism: Treats a group of agents as the unit of evolution, allowing discoveries from different branches to influence later designs. It aims to reuse exploratory diversity that would otherwise remain isolated in individual lineages.
evaluation: Evaluations use SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot, with model-transfer and framework-bug recovery analyses.
limitations: The evidence concerns coding agents under the study budgets. Curator interpretation: experience sharing during search is distinct from a deployed multi-agent team continually learning in an open environment.

title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Environment rewards evaluated under a fixed outer anchor.
mechanism: Uses a frozen model at three levels: task execution, harness editing, and editing the strategy used by the harness evolver. Each task family maintains a reusable evolving harness.
evaluation: BALROG experiments report gains on several game environments, held-out BabaIsAI sub-suites, and no improvement on NLE.
limitations: The authors identify limits from feedback quality and the frozen model capability. The outer anchor remains fixed, and held-out results concern the particular task-family splits.

title: Hyperagents
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Task evaluation and archived improvement histories, including transfer tests for the meta-agent.
mechanism: Combines the task solver and the agent that modifies it in one editable program. DGM-Hyperagents can therefore revise their own improvement procedure as well as task-solving code.
evaluation: The study includes coding, paper-review prediction, robotics reward design, and math-solution grading, with held-out task evaluations and cross-domain tests of the meta-agent.
limitations: The main experiments retain a fixed task distribution and outer selection/evaluation protocol. The paper establishes bounded transfer of improvement procedures, not unconstrained or indefinitely accelerating self-improvement.

title: HyperSkill: Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Hypergraph-Structured Skill Memory
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: Trajectory relationships and quality or utility signals used during memory maintenance.
mechanism: Connects reusable skills and subtask steps through trajectory-level hyperedges. Retrieval combines subtask and trajectory evidence, while periodic maintenance merges redundant skills and prunes low-utility entries.
evaluation: The authors compare memory baselines on xBench, GAIA, and WebWalkerQA with two language-model backbones.
limitations: This annotation is based on the primary abstract. Interpretation: benchmark comparisons do not independently establish long-term retention or safe pruning under changing task distributions.

title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Tests intrinsic correction: asking a model to revise its own reasoning using no external correctness signal.
evaluation: The studied reasoning settings show weak correction and, in some cases, degradation after revision.
limitations: The result concerns the tested models, prompts, and tasks; it does not rule out externally grounded feedback, learned correction, or durable agent learning.

title: LifelongAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Experience from earlier interactive tasks.
mechanism: Constructs interdependent tasks grounded in reusable skills across database, operating-system, and knowledge-graph environments.
evaluation: Tests experience reuse and a group self-consistency mechanism; ordinary replay is limited by irrelevant context and context length.
limitations: Performance on these task sequences should be separated from general lifelong learning. The abstract does not establish a complete audit of forgetting or long-term deployment.

title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents
code_note: Author-linked public repository page inspected; no installation, execution, or dataset download.
learning_signal: Accumulated interaction trajectories and language-model judgments of shared workflows and reusable skills.
mechanism: Clusters trajectories by procedural workflow, updates and splits clusters as experience grows, and distills transferable skills. Inference retrieves both environment-aligned examples and abstract skills without retraining the acting model.
evaluation: Uses ten environments across embodied action, tools, search, data analysis, and browsing, with 12,489 training and 1,230 test instances; measures performance, backward transfer, ablations, and two held-out transfer settings.
limitations: Experience construction includes model-generated and human-reviewed trajectories, rather than only autonomous deployment experience. Task order affects outcomes, and some domain/backbone combinations retain negative backward transfer. Million-experience deployment efficiency is not established.

title: Live-SWE-agent: Can Software Engineering Agents Self-Evolve on the Fly?
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Runtime observations while solving the current software-engineering problem.
mechanism: Starts with a minimal bash-based agent and permits edits to its own scaffold during task execution. It studies on-the-fly changes to the agent implementation without a separate offline evolution campaign.
evaluation: The authors report software-repair evaluations on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Pro.
limitations: The abstract establishes adaptation during a task, not durable learning carried between independent tasks. Current leaderboard rankings and results from different model versions should not be inferred from the paper.

title: Large Language Models as Tool Makers
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Task examples and feedback from producing and using generated tools.
mechanism: Separates tool creation from tool use, allowing a stronger model to create reusable programs that a cheaper model can invoke on related requests. A functional cache retains these capabilities across requests.
evaluation: The paper compares task accuracy and serving cost on reasoning problems, including BIG-Bench tasks.
limitations: Results depend on the selected task families and how tool-making costs are amortized. Interpretation: reusable tool creation does not establish unrestricted autonomous software evolution.

title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Builds extended conversations from persona and event structures, with human editing, to test recall, event summarization, and multimodal dialogue.
evaluation: Compares memory approaches on the LoCoMo conversational benchmark.
limitations: Recall from generated and edited conversations differs from learning a reusable procedure or improving an agent. Dataset statistics differ between paper and project versions; pin the artifact before comparing scores.

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Tests information extraction, cross-session and temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention from long interaction histories, separating indexing, retrieval, and reading.
evaluation: Evaluates memory designs and downstream question answering over controlled histories with scalable length.
limitations: Recall and evidence use are components of learning agents, not direct proof of procedural improvement. History version, reader, retrieval budget, and grader must be matched for comparisons.

title: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Evaluates whether memory systems recover environment-specific facts, state changes, workflows, pitfalls, and premise conditions from past web-agent trajectories.
evaluation: Compares retrieval and coding-agent evidence gathering on questions derived from specialized environments, including accuracy and latency tradeoffs.
limitations: This is a context-gathering and question-answering benchmark. Better answers do not alone demonstrate successful live task execution or sustained autonomous skill acquisition; the paper is marked work in progress.

title: Mem-α: Learning Memory Construction via Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: Question-answering accuracy over accumulated interaction history.
mechanism: Trains an agent to construct and update core, episodic, and semantic memory while processing sequential interaction chunks. Rewards come from answering questions over the full interaction history.
evaluation: The authors compare memory-augmented baselines and report generalization from training histories to substantially longer evaluation histories.
limitations: The abstract supports long-context memory construction under a QA objective. Interpretation: longer-context generalization should not be equated with cross-domain procedural learning or autonomous objective selection.

title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: Ongoing conversations and model-mediated fact extraction and consolidation.
mechanism: Extracts and consolidates facts from conversations for later retrieval, with a graph variant for relational information. Persistent conversational state provides a useful comparison point for more explicit experience-learning methods.
evaluation: The paper compares memory systems, retrieval approaches, and full-context baselines on LoCoMo using answer-quality, latency, and token-cost measures.
limitations: The reported evaluation concerns conversational recall and QA. The title’s production-readiness wording is an author characterization; this review does not establish deployment reliability or procedural self-improvement.

title: MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Author-linked public repository page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Downstream task-success rewards from complete agent interactions, plus selection-size and output-format penalties.
mechanism: Trains a memory-composition policy to choose the number, identity, and ordering of retrieved experiences. GRPO-based Experience Policy Optimization updates the composer while keeping the executor, retriever, and memory bank fixed.
evaluation: Reports three tau-squared-bench domains with 4B and 8B executors, memory-token costs, ordering ablations, and transfer across domains, executors, and memory sources.
limitations: This is external policy training, not continual growth of the memory bank. Frontier-scale executors and non-procedural memories are untested; sequence rewards confound selection and ordering, and several per-executor performance-gap confidence intervals include zero.

title: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
code_note: The author-linked Agent-on-the-Fly repository redirects to Memento-Teams/Memento; public page inspected, not executed.
learning_signal: Task outcomes attached to stored plans; the parametric variant trains a separate case-selection network from binary success feedback.
mechanism: A planner-executor agent stores completed cases and reuses them in subsequent planning. Retrieval can use fixed similarity or a learned Q-function; underlying LLM weights remain frozen, while the optional retrieval network changes.
evaluation: Reports deep-research and QA evaluations, memory ablations, and transfer. GAIA validation accumulates cases over three passes; the test run uses the validation-built case bank.
limitations: Validation Pass@3 and test accuracy use different protocols. The parametric variant performs gradient updates outside the LLM, so the whole system should not be described as parameter-free. Long-horizon Level 3 tasks remain difficult.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: Interaction history and agent-selected memory operations.
mechanism: Lets a language-model agent move information between a limited active context and external memory tiers through explicit operations. This supplies persistent state and self-managed context for later interactions.
evaluation: The authors evaluate document analysis beyond the active context window and memory across multiple chat sessions.
limitations: This is an adjacent memory architecture: remembered facts and context management do not alone establish accumulation of reusable task competence. Current software descended from the research may differ from the evaluated version.

title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: Downstream answer outcomes used for PPO and GRPO training.
mechanism: Trains a memory-management agent to add, update, delete, or retain entries, alongside an answer agent that selects and uses relevant memories. Outcome-driven reinforcement learning updates the policies governing external memory.
evaluation: The current abstract reports evaluation on LoCoMo, MSC, and LongMemEval across several model scales and question types.
limitations: Evidence reviewed here is the current abstract, not an audit of the training split or reward implementation. Conversation-memory QA gains do not establish improvement on long-horizon tool-use tasks.

title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: Past interactions, elapsed time, and assigned memory importance.
mechanism: Maintains retrievable interaction memories and user summaries, with time- and importance-sensitive forgetting and reinforcement. The SiliconFriend application combines this memory mechanism with a separately tuned conversational model.
evaluation: The paper combines qualitative user-dialogue analysis with quantitative tests on model-generated long-term conversations.
limitations: Simulated dialogue and personalization outcomes are not clinical validation or evidence of general task-skill improvement. The memory mechanism should be distinguished from separate model tuning.

title: Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Past execution trajectories and feedback used to correct or deprecate procedures.
mechanism: Distills trajectories into both detailed instructions and more abstract procedures. Its procedural-memory pipeline builds, retrieves, revises, and retires entries as further experience arrives.
evaluation: The paper studies TravelPlanner and ALFWorld and reports transfer of procedural memory from a stronger model to a weaker one.
limitations: The reported gains concern analogous tasks in two benchmark environments. Interpretation: cross-model reuse does not by itself demonstrate transfer to unrelated task families or indefinite retention.

title: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Environment feedback updates the utility assigned to episodic memories.
mechanism: Uses outcome feedback to adjust the utility of episodic memories while keeping the reasoning model fixed. Two-stage retrieval combines semantic relevance with learned utility to select useful past strategies.
evaluation: The authors report results on HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, and Lifelong Agent Bench.
limitations: The abstract and official repository were inspected; training/evaluation separation and statistical uncertainty were not independently audited. Benchmark gains do not settle the stability-plasticity problem in general.

title: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution
code_note: Current author repository inspected; it points to a separate mce-artifact repository for paper experiments. Not executed.
learning_signal: Training rollouts and validation utility for candidate context functions and their engineering skills.
mechanism: A meta-agent revises context-engineering skills; a base agent executes them to construct context as files and code. History-informed evolutionary selection retains useful context functions and corresponding skills.
evaluation: Tests finance, chemistry, medicine, law, and safety-classification datasets, with offline and online variants and component ablations.
limitations: Full iterative skill evolution applies to offline experiments; single-pass online processing uses a different variant. The authors identify reasoning-heavy tasks and long, complex trajectories as limitations. Domain tests do not establish clinical or legal validity.

title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Recursive resampling and training on prior-generation model outputs.
mechanism: Analyzes how repeated training on generated data can lose low-probability parts of an original distribution and amplify errors. The paper combines tractable distribution models with generative-model experiments.
evaluation: Experiments include Gaussian mixtures, variational autoencoders, and repeated language-model fine-tuning, with differing amounts of original data retained.
limitations: The theoretical replacement setting and finite experiments have specific data-mixing assumptions. Curator interpretation: this is a warning about recursive data use, not a proof that every verified or data-accumulating self-learning loop must fail.

title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Models an agent as a foundation model plus prompts, memory, tools, and control logic, organizing self-induced updates by their target and learning signal.
evaluation: Synthesizes model and scaffold adaptation, applications, and evaluation problems.
limitations: A survey’s deployment discussion is not independent deployment validation. Different update mechanisms still require different controls and measures.

title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Contrasts between successful and failed trajectories, followed by validation gates.
mechanism: Evolves five harness modules in separate restricted lineages, then integrates their changes. The evolved agent performs trajectory analysis and code modification; a function library controls reuse and redundancy.
evaluation: Evolution uses a separately constructed task collection; the frozen learned library is evaluated on TerminalBench 2.0 and SWE-bench Verified, including cross-model transfer.
limitations: The reported benchmark separation depends on the documented curation and similarity-screening procedure. Infrastructure is outside the editable scope, and downstream evaluation allows function selection but no further function modification.

title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation
code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
learning_signal: Accumulated skill-use experience and feedback from evaluating created skills.
mechanism: Manages a skill lifecycle spanning creation, storage, retrieval, evaluation, and refinement. Per-skill experience persists across tasks so later attempts can reuse and adapt earlier work.
evaluation: The revised abstract reports SkillsBench and SkillLearnBench comparisons and transfer of generated skills to another agent.
limitations: The comparison with human-authored skills is explicitly reported on a successfully covered subset. Interpretation: that subset result should not be presented as an overall advantage across all tasks.

title: OpenSIR: Open-Ended Self-Improving Reasoner
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Difficulty calibration and diversity rewards for self-generated problems.
mechanism: Alternates teacher and student roles within one model, starting from a seed problem. The method rewards exploration of distinct concepts while keeping generated tasks within a learnable difficulty range.
evaluation: The current paper reports mathematical benchmark improvements for instruction and reasoning models and transfer to selected general-reasoning evaluations.
limitations: The paper’s open-ended framing should be read against its finite training runs and benchmark suite. This abstract-level review does not establish correctness of all generated problems or unbounded discovery.

title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Scores of earlier candidate prompts on a development task.
mechanism: Uses an LLM to propose candidates from a history of instructions and their measured scores. Selected instructions can be reused on new examples without changing model weights.
evaluation: Prompt optimization is evaluated on GSM8K and BIG-Bench Hard, alongside illustrative numerical and combinatorial optimization tasks.
limitations: This is an external prompt-search procedure, not evidence of autonomous lifelong agent learning. Curator interpretation: the chosen objective and development data constrain what the search can improve.

title: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Paired candidate/incumbent correctness on development instances.
mechanism: Places a sequential statistical gate between proposed prompt edits and retention. A betting-based evidence process accepts an edit only after its paired outcomes cross a threshold; otherwise the incumbent remains.
evaluation: Author experiments use Qwen2.5 prompt evolution on GSM8K, SVAMP, and ARC-Challenge, with planted-gain and stochastic regimes and a separate audit pool. Statistical gates reduce noisy commitments relative to greedy selection.
limitations: The guarantee is per candidate under a conditional paired-null assumption, not a guarantee for the whole adaptive search. Experiments cover one model family and prompt edits; the finite audit and development-set coverage limit interpretation. Small genuine gains may be rejected.

title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
learning_signal: Earlier task experience and explicit state updates; controls remove or corrupt retained information.
mechanism: Uses ordered fresh-session tasks with matched retention-on and retention-off conditions, and records evidence for saving, retrieving, and updating persistent state.
evaluation: Tests personal-agent frameworks across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering, and update, with diagnostic interventions in Hermes+.
limitations: The controlled families and model-dependent gains test prerequisites for recursive improvement, not an open-ended recursive process. Task scores and intended mechanism evidence are separate outcomes.

title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Runs frozen-model controls through the same pipeline as self-training to estimate how decoding and measurement noise can create apparent per-problem capability changes.
evaluation: Audits repeated low-rank self-training and matched alternatives, proposing per-problem tests against pooled baseline replicates.
limitations: The reported measurement failures are valuable controls for study design; results from one training setup do not establish that every self-training method fails.

title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Fitness on task examples guides selection of task prompts and mutation prompts.
mechanism: Evolves a population of task instructions together with the instructions that produce their mutations. It provides a concrete example of changing part of the improvement procedure as well as the task-solving prompt.
evaluation: Evaluations cover arithmetic, commonsense reasoning, and hate-speech classification.
limitations: The foundation model and surrounding evolutionary procedure remain fixed. Prompt-level self-reference should not be read as evidence of unbounded improvement of the complete agent.

title: R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Challenger rewards for tasks near the solver’s capability boundary and solver rewards on generated tasks.
mechanism: Initializes challenger and solver models from the same base model, then optimizes their roles separately. Their interaction generates an adaptive training curriculum without a pre-existing task-and-label dataset.
evaluation: The authors report mathematical and general-domain reasoning improvements across multiple backbone models.
limitations: The framework still depends on pretrained models and the designed reward procedure. This abstract-level review does not independently validate generated task correctness, long-run stability, or open-world transfer.

title: RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
learning_signal: Environment rewards on multi-turn trajectories, with reward variability and gradient diagnostics guiding stabilization.
mechanism: StarPO optimizes reasoning-action trajectories with reinforcement learning. The study identifies repetitive reasoning collapse and tests StarPO-S interventions including rollout filtering, a critic, and gradient stabilization.
evaluation: Version 2 studies Bandit, Sokoban, FrozenLake, and WebShop, varying optimization, rollout design, rewards, and generalization conditions.
limitations: The paper reports small-scale tasks and no multimodal evaluation. Better rewards do not guarantee meaningful reasoning. The linked repository now includes RAGEN-2 and additional environments; its current branch is not a pinned reproduction of this paper.

title: Re-ReST: Reflection-Reinforced Self-Training for Language Agents
code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
learning_signal: External training-time feedback such as answer correctness, environment outcomes, and unit tests.
mechanism: Trains a separate reflector to repair unsuccessful model-generated examples. Accepted original and repaired trajectories then fine-tune the agent, so improvement is retained in its parameters; the main inference path needs only the trained agent.
evaluation: Experiments cover multi-hop question answering, ALFWorld, code generation, visual question answering, and image generation, with reflector and preference-training analyses.
limitations: Feedback and task inputs are supplied during training. The reflector shares the model family but not weights with the agent. A separate self-consistency inference variant should not be confused with the main training-only use of reflection.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Environment observations during task execution.
mechanism: Interleaves reasoning traces with actions and observations so a language model can gather information and revise its plan during a task.
evaluation: Experiments cover question answering, fact verification, ALFWorld, and WebShop with comparisons to reasoning-only and acting-only approaches.
limitations: Included as a baseline agent loop. The prompted interaction loop does not itself establish persistent self-learning between tasks.

title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Self-judged task outcomes and contrasts among multiple execution trajectories.
mechanism: Extracts reusable reasoning lessons from self-judged successful and failed trajectories and retrieves them for later tasks. Memory-aware test-time scaling adds diverse attempts to improve the experience available for consolidation.
evaluation: The study evaluates sequential web-browsing and software-engineering tasks, with memory baselines, failure-trajectory ablations, and test-time-compute comparisons.
limitations: The learning signal relies on model judgments rather than access to ground truth during the task stream. Interpretation: memory gains should be compared under matched compute budgets, task order, and protection against retrieving the current task’s answer.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Scalar or textual environment feedback, exact-match grading, heuristics, and model-generated evaluation, depending on the experiment.
mechanism: Converts task feedback into verbal reflections and carries those reflections into later attempts through an episodic memory buffer. The underlying language-model weights stay fixed.
evaluation: The study evaluates repeated attempts on ALFWorld, HotpotQA, and programming tasks, with ablations of reflection and feedback.
limitations: The central experiments improve retries of the same task; they do not establish a durable cross-task learning library. Feedback sources differ by task, and the paper uses bounded memory.

title: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
venue: Author reports NeurIPS 2026 CLEA workshop acceptance; venue record not independently verified.
code_note: An official implementation was not independently verified in this review; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Completed trajectories supply structured experience; a hand-written in-loop struggle signal controls when detailed records enter context.
mechanism: Consolidates past coding traces into phased documents, injects a retrieved document at task start, and exposes a detailed implementation record only when the agent struggles. The detailed record is evicted after one exposure.
evaluation: Studies 99 SWE-ContextBench Lite tasks, with three replicates for the principal Sonnet 4.5 conditions, retrieval comparisons, ablations, and additional model contrasts.
limitations: Experiments reuse a fixed experience pool rather than an online-growing memory. Recall-policy contrasts do not reach p<0.05 at this sample size; several secondary conditions run once. Retrieval baselines use different configurations, and stronger agents can be harmed by memory. All tasks retrieve same-repository experience; similarity to gold patches was not measured.

title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: A reward-based training objective applied to batches sampled from the current policy.
mechanism: Alternates generating a batch of candidate outputs and improving the policy with offline reinforcement learning. Reusing generated data reduces the need to sample a new online batch for every update.
evaluation: The reported experiments focus on machine translation, assessed using automatic metrics and human evaluation.
limitations: This is externally organized model training on a specific application. Curator interpretation: the study does not establish a lifelong agent or a reward signal that itself improves without outside specification.

title: ReST-MCTS*: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Known final answers and search-derived estimates of intermediate-step value.
mechanism: Combines process-reward-guided tree search with iterative training of the policy and reward models. Search supplies reasoning traces and step-value targets without requiring human labels for every intermediate step.
evaluation: The authors compare search methods at matched search budgets and report multi-iteration self-training results for three language models.
limitations: Oracle final answers remain available, and inferred step rewards depend on the search procedure. Curator interpretation: removing manual process labels does not remove external supervision.

title: Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Answer correctness and improved responses from self-distillation or a stronger teacher.
mechanism: Turns single-turn problems into multi-turn trajectories and trains the model to revise earlier unsuccessful responses. Its training loop uses reward-weighted supervised learning over the current model’s attempts and improved continuations.
evaluation: Math-reasoning experiments compare sequential improvement with single-turn strategies under comparable inference budgets and examine iterative training and distribution shift.
limitations: The learned correction policy persists in weights, while the revisions at deployment concern the current problem. Some data-collection variants use a stronger model; this is not recursive modification of the learning algorithm itself.

title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Not applicable: a study of reported evaluation designs.
mechanism: Codes whether self-improvement studies evaluate final artifacts, repeat the entire learning loop, or compare earlier and later improvers from identical starting artifacts at matched budgets.
evaluation: The authors analyze 114 eligible studies from an arXiv phrase-based search frozen on 17 October 2026, including 90 RSI-labeled studies. Only four of 26 improver claimants report the specified same-start comparison; separate human coding checks selected evidence.
limitations: This measures reporting within a restricted literature frame, not the success rate of all self-improving agents. AI-assisted coding outside the adjudicated sample and improver-comparison set was not individually human-checked; coding disagreements materially affect estimates.

title: Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Uses a transition-centered framework to examine how reusable state acquires influence, changes scope, and propagates failures through later adaptations.
evaluation: Reviews evidence for admission, retrieval, activation, containment, and repair; identifies comparatively weak evidence for repairing descendants and evaluating resumed learning.
limitations: The framework proposes how to organize longitudinal safety assessment; it does not certify that a learning system remains safe.

title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Online rewards and regularization over self-generated multi-turn correction traces.
mechanism: Trains a correction policy on its own response distribution, with an initialization stage and a reward bonus encouraging successful revision. The method targets distribution mismatch and collapsed correction behavior observed in offline supervised training.
evaluation: The authors evaluate self-correction on MATH and HumanEval using Gemini models.
limitations: The training produces a reusable correction capability; a test-time revision is still a within-problem operation. Curator interpretation: these benchmarks do not show autonomous lifelong improvement across changing environments.

title: Self-Adapting Language Models
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Downstream performance after applying a generated self-edit.
mechanism: Learns to generate synthetic training material or adaptation directives, then applies gradient updates using those edits. An outer reward-based loop improves the edit-generation policy while an inner loop adapts the model.
evaluation: Experiments cover knowledge incorporation and few-shot ARC adaptation; the paper also tests retention after sequential knowledge edits.
limitations: ARC evaluation uses a small subset selected for solvability under suitable adaptation settings. Sequential edits still show forgetting, and evaluating each candidate edit requires model tuning; the paper does not establish stable lifelong adaptation.

title: Self-Challenging Language Model Agents
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Self-generated task verification functions and tests, followed by task-evaluation rewards.
mechanism: The agent first explores supplied tools as a challenger and constructs Code-as-Task problems containing instructions, a verifier, and passing and failing examples. It then learns as an executor through reinforcement learning on the filtered generated tasks.
evaluation: The authors evaluate multi-turn tool use on M3ToolEval and TauBench.
limitations: Tool interfaces and the learning framework are supplied externally. Curator interpretation: tests of a generated verifier cannot establish that every generated task captures its intended semantics or that gains transfer to arbitrary tools.

title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Separates self-correction questions by feedback source and training assumptions, and examines whether experimental designs support the claimed correction ability.
evaluation: The reviewed evidence favors reliable external feedback or trained correction in many settings, while questioning broad claims for prompted intrinsic correction.
limitations: This is a review of the literature available in 2024, not a universal impossibility theorem or a measurement of current models.

title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
learning_signal: Environment task-success feedback used by the evaluated evolvers; held-out checkpoint tests measure retention and interference.
mechanism: Evaluates frozen-model agents that update retrieved experience, a shared prompt, or harness files on drifting streams. It separates gains on current tasks from interference with unseen families and forgetting of earlier ones.
evaluation: ReasoningBank, GEPA, and Meta-Harness are compared with a common Gemini 3.6 Flash backbone on four streams built from BIRD, BFCL, and ScienceWorld, with disjoint held-out evaluations.
limitations: Findings concern these implementations, one backbone, and constructed drift schedules. The retrieval baseline always injects its nearest memory without a similarity threshold; global edits and conflicting workflows expose different failure modes, not a universal impossibility result.

title: Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents
code_note: Author-linked repository and setup documentation inspected; not installed or executed.
learning_signal: An external judge flags harmful completed trajectories; model components synthesize and organize defensive policies.
mechanism: Stores failure episodes and distills them into a hierarchical policy memory. Relevant policies condition later tasks while the acting model stays frozen.
evaluation: The authors evaluate eight benchmarks spanning jailbreaks, prompt injection, and coding, plus adaptive attackers and a frozen-memory control. Each benchmark starts with empty memory; updates occur only after completed episodes.
limitations: The reported protocol does not establish cross-benchmark retention. Retrieval and enforcement failures remain, and learning depends on the external judge. DTap additionally uses a pre-tool guard, which must be retained when interpreting comparisons.

title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
mechanism: Organizes agent adaptation by the component that changes, the stage when it changes, the feedback and algorithm used, and the application setting.
evaluation: Synthesizes published methods, benchmarks, and open questions rather than evaluating one new learner.
limitations: A taxonomy is an organizing aid, not evidence that every included system improves continually. The title’s superintelligence framing is a research aspiration.

title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Model-generated instruction/input/output examples filtered for invalidity and similarity.
mechanism: Bootstraps an instruction-tuning dataset from the model, filters unsuitable examples, and fine-tunes the original model on the retained data. It is a foundation for synthetic-data learning rather than a deployed agent that learns during use.
evaluation: The paper evaluates instruction following on Super-NaturalInstructions and expert-written novel tasks, including human assessment.
limitations: The generator inherits its pretrained capabilities and biases, and dataset filtering is part of the learning system. Curator interpretation: better instruction following alone is not evidence of continual agent learning.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Model-generated feedback on the current answer.
mechanism: Uses the same language model to draft, critique, and revise an answer iteratively without updating model weights.
evaluation: The paper compares iterative refinement with one-shot generation on several generation and reasoning tasks using human and automatic assessments.
limitations: These are within-task output improvements. They do not establish retained learning on later tasks, and the evaluation conditions differ from studies of intrinsic reasoning correction.

title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: The language model judges candidate responses to construct preferences for iterative DPO.
mechanism: Uses one language model both to answer instructions and to score responses, updating it through successive rounds of preference optimization. This couples the response generator and the source of training rewards.
evaluation: The paper reports instruction-following and reward-quality improvements across three iterations, including AlpacaEval 2.0 evaluation.
limitations: The evidence concerns bounded iterations and selected evaluation protocols. Curator interpretation: agreement with an evolving self-judge is not an independent guarantee of correctness or indefinite improvement.

title: SelfOp: An Optimization Algorithm for Self-Improving Security Agents
code_note: Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.
learning_signal: Execution outcomes, vulnerability metadata, and cross-instance agreement among textual critiques.
mechanism: Traces errors backward through outcomes, trajectories, and context, then clusters critiques to revise persistent skill instructions and reference documents. Model weights and the execution harness remain fixed.
evaluation: Studies CyberGym vulnerability reproduction, component ablations, checkpoint selection, and cross-model transfer; the held-out test subset contains 80 tasks.
limitations: Evaluation covers a cost-limited benchmark subset. Baselines are adapted to shared supervision. Stopping avoids validation during the final optimization run, but its noise floor and window were empirically calibrated using earlier runs with validation scoring. Other security tasks remain future work.

title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
code_note: Official repository linked in the paper and landing page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Benchmark feedback and LLM reflection on candidate code changes.
mechanism: Equips a coding agent with tools to edit its own implementation and reuses improved versions in later iterations. Learning changes the surrounding agent code rather than model parameters.
evaluation: The paper reports gains on a random SWE-bench Verified subset, LiveCodeBench, and synthetic agent tasks.
limitations: The software-repair result uses a fixed 50-task subset and a five-minute timeout. The authors note that faster file editing explains part of the gain, with limited improvements on reasoning tasks; repeated benchmark evaluation is distinct from held-out deployment transfer.

title: SkillFlow:Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Trajectories, task outcomes, and evaluation rubrics.
mechanism: Starts agents without skills and carries a library of trajectory- and rubric-derived skill patches through sequential tasks within task families.
evaluation: Measures task success, skill discovery, revision, and reuse across a structured set of task families, with benefits differing substantially across models.
limitations: Skill invocation is not evidence of useful learning: the paper reports high use with small gains or regression. Family-specific evaluation does not establish broad transfer.

title: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
venue: NeurIPS 2026 acceptance reported by authors; venue record not inspected
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Task rewards, teacher-generated skill distillation, and validation failures.
mechanism: Distills successful and failed trajectories into a hierarchical skill library, retrieves those skills during policy training, and adds lessons from validation failures. The library and model policy change together during reinforcement learning.
