evaluation: The authors evaluate ALFWorld, WebShop, and seven search-augmented QA datasets, including component and teacher-model analyses.
limitations: The method uses a teacher and reward-bearing environments, so it is not training-free or supervision-free. Interpretation: its recursive skill refresh is not evidence that the system can redesign its own learning algorithm.

title: Socratic-Zero : Bootstrapping Reasoning via Data-Free Agent Co-evolution
code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
learning_signal: A fixed stronger teacher's correctness judgments, reference solutions, and failure-targeted generated problems.
mechanism: Updates a solver through online preference learning and trains a generator to imitate useful teacher-generated curricula. The teacher remains frozen while the solver and generator change.
evaluation: The authors compare solver accuracy on seven mathematical and three general-reasoning benchmarks and assess synthetic data through downstream student training.
limitations: Despite the title, experiments use 100 MATH seed questions, initial supervised tuning on 1,500 problems, and a Qwen3-235B teacher. Mean@32 evaluation and teacher-derived judgments should be preserved when interpreting comparisons; this is not learning without prior data or an external teacher.

title: SPICE: Self-Play In Corpus Environments Improves Reasoning
code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
learning_signal: Document-extracted answers, answer-equivalence checks, and a reward favoring tasks near the solver's capability frontier.
mechanism: A shared model alternates between a document-grounded challenger and a reasoner without document access. Role-specific reinforcement-learning updates improve question generation and solving together.
evaluation: Four Qwen and OctoThinker base models are tested on mathematics and general-reasoning suites, with corpus, task-format, and challenger-reward ablations.
limitations: Experiments use a selected 20,000-document corpus and a fixed training horizon. Curator interpretation: dependence on document quality, generated answers, and verification remains; these experiments do not establish indefinite improvement.

title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Contrasts previous-model responses with existing human demonstrations.
mechanism: Starts with a supervised model and iteratively learns to distinguish its own generated responses from reference demonstrations. Successive model versions provide the changing opponent in the training objective.
evaluation: The authors report results on Open LLM Leaderboard tasks, MT-Bench, and Big-Bench datasets.
limitations: No additional human annotation is required by the loop, but existing human demonstrations remain its target distribution. Curator interpretation: this is not learning from zero prior human data.

title: SPIRAL: Self-Play on Zero-Sum Games Incentivizes Reasoning via Multi-Agent Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
learning_signal: Terminal game outcomes and role-conditioned advantage estimates.
mechanism: One shared language-model policy plays both sides of zero-sum games and receives online policy-gradient updates. Separate baselines for each role stabilize training as the opposing policy improves.
evaluation: The study trains on TicTacToe, Kuhn Poker, and Simple Negotiation and evaluates transfer to mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks across several Qwen and Llama configurations.
limitations: The curriculum depends on engineered games and pretrained models. The authors report substantial compute, training plateaus, and limited academic-benchmark transfer evidence; game rewards can favor strategies other than the intended reasoning skill.

title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Known correct answers filter generated rationales; answer hints support rationalization of failed examples.
mechanism: Generates reasoning traces, keeps traces ending in the reference answer, and fine-tunes on them. Failed problems can be retried with the answer supplied as a hint; each outer iteration retrains from the original base model on the newly collected traces.
evaluation: Experiments cover arithmetic, CommonsenseQA, and GSM8K, with comparisons to direct-answer fine-tuning and prompted reasoning.
limitations: The method needs training questions, reference answers, and a small rationale seed. Correct final answers do not independently certify that every intermediate explanation is valid.

title: Learn Now, Use Next, Trust Later: Prequential Test-Time Learning for LLM Agents
code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
learning_signal: Observed action transitions and prospective checks of predicted effects in later, non-source episodes.
mechanism: Extracts testable policy hypotheses that can guide the next decision, while keeping persistent reuse behind an evidence gate. Candidate predictions are frozen before later observations; counterevidence can withdraw promoted guidance. Model weights remain fixed.
evaluation: The paper compares two actor configurations and learning baselines across five rounds on WebArena-Lite and ALFWorld, including first-attempt analysis, safeguards ablations, and costs.
limitations: Evaluation repeats tasks and excludes ten WebArena-Lite cases. Promotion relies on environment-specific evidence adapters; predictive validation does not by itself establish causal policy utility. Longer changing streams remain future work.

title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
learning_signal: Utility functions scoring the programs produced by an improver.
mechanism: Begins with an LLM-assisted program improver and applies that improver to its own source. Candidate improvers are assessed through the quality of programs they generate for downstream tasks.
evaluation: The study reports improvements on a small set of algorithmic tasks and separately examines attempts to bypass a sandbox.
limitations: The authors explicitly retain a fixed language model, so the result is bounded scaffold self-improvement. Performance on the small task set does not establish an indefinitely accelerating process.

title: Symbolic Learning Enables Self-Evolving Agents
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Natural-language representations of losses and gradients derived from task outcomes.
mechanism: Represents an agent as a symbolic network whose editable components include prompts, tools, and their composition. Symbolic optimization uses textual feedback to revise that network.
evaluation: The abstract describes proof-of-concept experiments on standard benchmarks and more complex tasks.
limitations: These are natural-language analogues of gradient-based learning, not mathematical derivatives of a differentiable objective. The reviewed abstract does not establish unrestricted long-term learning after deployment.

title: Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models: Decoupling Chosen-Rejected via Past-Future
code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
learning_signal: Preferences using anchored past-model rejections and newer-model chosen responses.
mechanism: Separates the model generations used to provide rejected and chosen samples so their learning signal does not shrink as both improve together. The paper applies this temporal arrangement to iterative self-rewarding training.
evaluation: The authors compare model families and sizes at matched compute and report instruction-following and selected out-of-distribution reasoning, QA, and coding results.
limitations: This review inspected the proceedings abstract and repository landing page. Curator interpretation: reported task transfer does not establish a calibrated self-judge or unlimited improvement over future generations.

title: TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text
venue: Nature 2025; journal title: Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback
code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
learning_signal: Natural-language critiques propagated through a computation graph.
mechanism: Treats components of a compound AI system as editable variables and routes textual feedback backward to propose updates. Applications include reusable prompt optimization and refinement of individual outputs.
evaluation: The paper reports studies in question answering, code generation, molecule design, and treatment-plan optimization.
limitations: Output refinement and reusable system learning are different experimental settings. Curator interpretation: success under an LLM critic does not by itself establish correctness or clinical validity.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
learning_signal: Self-supervised tool-use examples seeded by a small number of demonstrations for each API.
mechanism: Teaches a language model when to call a predefined API, which arguments to produce, and how to incorporate the returned information. The learned capability is stored in model parameters rather than a growing tool library.
evaluation: The paper evaluates zero-shot downstream tasks using tools such as a calculator, question answering, search, translation, and a calendar.
limitations: The available APIs and initial demonstrations are supplied by researchers. Curator interpretation: learning to invoke these tools is distinct from autonomously creating new tools or learning continually after deployment.

title: TroVE: Inducing Verifiable and Efficient Toolboxes for Solving Programmatic Tasks
code_note: Official repository linked by the paper and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Agreement among executed candidate outputs, program simplicity, and observed tool reuse.
mechanism: Samples solutions that import existing functions, create new ones, or use only supplied primitives. Execution agreement and simplicity select a solution whose functions join a reusable toolbox; periodic trimming removes low-use functions without model training.
evaluation: Tests 11 math, table-QA, and visual-reasoning datasets. A separate study asks six people to verify 100 table-QA solutions and measures verification time and accuracy.
limitations: Supplied primitives and demonstrations constrain the tool space. Agreement is not proof of correctness, and the human study does not establish universal reliability. Some comparisons reuse previously reported baseline scores.

title: Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks
code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
learning_signal: Benchmark feedback during the self-modification process.
mechanism: Studies whether poisoned optimization benchmarks can induce persistent changes that cause self-modifying coding agents to emit vulnerable code on later clean tasks.
evaluation: Presents proof-of-concept studies on a modified Darwin Gödel Machine, SICA, and Hyperagents, including continued evolution after poison removal.
limitations: These are constructed attacks under specified agent and benchmark conditions, not an estimate of attack prevalence. Clean subsequent tasks do not reliably remove contaminated components in the studied cases.

title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
code_note: Official repository and README inspected; released harnesses and result files were not independently audited or executed.
learning_signal: Executed draft checks, failure replay and perturbation, training regressions, and validation summaries.
mechanism: Updates an executor harness and the optimizer's own prompts, skills, tools, hooks, and notes. Verification tools test proposed fixes and diagnoses before submission while both models remain frozen.
evaluation: Adds VERSE to four reimplemented harness optimizers, evaluating held-out SWE-rebench and newer multilingual tasks; also studies Terminal-Bench and component ablations.
limitations: Selection rules and core verification tools remain fixed. Matched candidate counts do not imply equal total compute. Reimplemented baselines differ from their original systems; self-evolution benefits vary by host, and noisy outcome changes often fail to reproduce.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
learning_signal: Environment observations, interpreter errors, and model-based task verification.
mechanism: Builds an expanding library of executable Minecraft skills, retrieved and composed for later tasks. An automatic curriculum proposes objectives, while execution feedback and a model-based critic guide program repair before a skill is retained.
evaluation: The authors compare exploration, technology-tree progress, ablations, and reuse of learned skills on new tasks in another Minecraft world.
limitations: Results concern a simulator with supplied control APIs. The paper reports inaccurate self-verification and impossible proposed tasks, so its retained library is not guaranteed correct.

title: From Static Templates to Dynamic Runtime Graphs: A Survey of Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents
code_note: Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.
learning_signal: Not applicable: literature synthesis and evaluation framework.
mechanism: Organizes workflow optimization by when structure is determined, which components change, and which feedback governs changes. Separates reusable templates, per-run graphs, and execution traces.
evaluation: Proposes reporting that combines downstream task performance with structural properties, cost, robustness, and variation across inputs.
limitations: A taxonomy and reporting proposal do not independently validate surveyed methods. Runtime graph changes can be specific to one task and should not automatically be interpreted as persistent learning.
